one_liner: Julia SIMD xoshiro-style RNG with vectorized Box-Muller; about 2x Julia's old dSFMT MersenneTwister for randn! (1.5-3.4x for rand!).
what_it_does: VectorizedRNG.jl is a Julia package that fills arrays with uniform (rand!) and normal (randn!) Float64/Float32 values, and UInt64 values, from many SIMD-parallel xoshiro streams. You get a per-thread generator with local_rng() (or a standalone MutableXoshiro(seed)) and pass it to the standard Random.rand!/randn! functions, so it plugs into Julia's AbstractRNG interface. rand!/randn! also accept (α, β, γ) to compute x = α·x + γ·z + β in place, and scalar rand()/randn() draws are served from a 256-value buffer. It is Julia only and has no C or C++ interface.
how_it_is_fast: Each thread owns XREGISTERS = 2 SIMD registers of independent xoshiro-style states, so 8 streams on AVX2 or 16 on AVX-512, spaced by the xoshiro256 2^128 jump polynomial. A bulk fill advances all lanes at once with integer shift/xor/rotate vector ops, converts bits to floats with mask tricks (vpternlog on AVX-512), and writes two vectors per loop iteration with masked tail stores. Normals come from a SIMD Box-Muller transform using Remez-fitted polynomial sin/cos and log approximations, whereas Julia's MersenneTwister randn uses a scalar ziggurat; the README credits most of the randn! gain to this.
when_to_use: Julia code filling medium Float64 arrays (around 1024 elements, the size benchmarked) with normals, where the README shows 7.235 us to 3.744 us on AVX2 Haswell and 1.676 us to 854 ns on an AVX-512 i7-1165G7
AVX-512 x86 machines, where uniform rand! went from 549.9 ns to 159.9 ns (about 3.4x, derived from page data)
Monte Carlo kernels that need in-place scaled noise via randn!(rng, x, StaticInt(0), β, γ), i.e. x = γ·z + β without a temporary
Statistical work where per-thread streams are enough and bit reproducibility across machines is not needed
when_not_to_use: Anything that needs a C or C++ library: this is a Julia package built on VectorizationBase.jl and SLEEFPirates.jl

Code that relies on the documented xoshiro256++ algorithm, its period or its 2^128 stream spacing: src/xoshiro.jl drops the '+ s0' output term and rotates s3 right by 45 (a left rotation by 19, not 45), so it is a nonstandard variant and the reused xoshiro256 jump constants do not establish stream separation

Current Julia (1.7+): the README's baseline is the old dSFMT MersenneTwister; Julia's default RNG is now a per-task Xoshiro256++ with its own SIMD bulk path (Julia Random docs, seen only via search snippets), and no comparison against it is published
Apple M1/NEON: open issue #20 reports randn! at about 2.85 us vs 1.69 us for the default RNG (about 69% slower) and no faster rand!

Large arrays that spill out of cache, or long-term maintenance: issue #4 argues the gain fades beyond about 2048 elements, and VectorizationBase.jl's README says it is 'looking for new maintainers, otherwise deprecated in Julia 1.11'

integration.dependencies: VectorizationBase.jl (0.19.38, 0.20.1 or 0.21), SLEEFPirates.jl 0.6.29+, UnPack.jl, Random, Distributed, Requires; optional StaticArraysCore extension
integration.platforms: x86-64 best (AVX2, AVX-512 where it shines); aarch64 NEON runs but is slower than Base for randn! per issue #20; vector width picked by VectorizationBase at load
integration.thread_safety: One generator per thread via local_rng(), indexed by Threads.threadid() into a block allocated for Threads.nthreads() when the package loads; a single generator must not be shared between threads, and task migration or threads added after load are not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: implements Random.AbstractRNG so rand!/randn!/rand work, but you must pass local_rng() explicitly, Random.seed! does not seed it (use VectorizedRNG.seed!), and the output stream differs from Base

gotchas: Bug in the scaled in-place path: when α is passed as an ordinary number (anything other than StaticInt(0)), the main loop of samplevector! in src/api.jl line 266 uses z₁ for the second vector, so each pair of adjacent W-element chunks gets identical random draws; only the tail block uses z₂. The default rand!/randn! (α = StaticInt(0)) path is correct, and the test only checks the mean, so it does not catch this.
Seeding is separate from Base: the generator is seeded from Base's global RNG at load time, Random.seed! has no effect, and VectorizedRNG.seed!(n) reseeds every thread's streams at once.
Results depend on SIMD width and thread count: streams are interleaved across 8 (AVX2) or 16 (AVX-512) lanes per thread, so the same seed gives different sequences on different machines.

The README itself reports that its BigCrush run on a 10980XE was slower than MersenneTwister's (511.5 s vs 481.8 s) and warns 'Watch out when mixing vectorized and non-vectorized code' (AVX-512 downclocking).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this only inside Julia, where it is the ready-made SIMD normal and uniform filler. From C++, simdrng gives verified lane-correct xoshiro256++ with SIMD bulk fill, and EigenRand or the normaldist-benchmark Box-Muller code cover vectorized normals; simd-rand is the Rust equivalent.
verified_claims_summary: The README's BenchmarkTools minimum times for filling a 1024-element Vector{Float64} compare Base's then-default dSFMT MersenneTwister with local_rng(): randn! 7.235 us vs 3.744 us and rand! 791 ns vs 513 ns on an unspecified AVX2 Haswell, and randn! 1.676 us vs 854 ns and rand! 549.9 ns vs 159.9 ns on an Intel i7-1165G7 (AVX-512) under Julia 1.6.0-DEV.1581 with LLVM 11. No C++ std:: baseline is involved, and Julia's current Xoshiro-based default was not measured.
